extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner procedures for preparing, filing, and processing Information Disclosure Statements (IDSs) under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 and MPEP §609. Covers timing, contents, required copies/translations, examiner consideration, printing, and related procedural consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirements under 37 CFR 1.97 (initial window)
rubrics_metrics.description: "(1)(a) for national applications (not including CPAs), within 3 months of filing or before first Office action on the merits, whichever is later; (b) for national stage applications, within 3 months of entry into national stage or before first Office action on the merits, whichever is later; (c) for RCEs and CPAs before the first Office action on the merits." (MPEP 609.01)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDSs may be filed without statement or fees if within these initial time windows; timing is based on the filing of the IDS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirements after initial window but before final/allowance/Quayle
rubrics_metrics.description: If filed after the initial period but before final action, notice of allowance, or Quayle action, an 1.97(e) statement or payment of the 1.17(p) fee is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP 609.01; filing during this period changes what statements/fees are required for the IDS to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing requirements when filed after that but before or with issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If filed after the previous window and before (or with) payment of the issue fee, an 1.97(e) statement and the 1.17(p) fee are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDS filed at this stage requires both the statement and fee for consideration; MPEP 609.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS filed after payment of issue fee will not be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed after payment of the issue fee will not be considered by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MPEP 609.01 — applicants should not expect post-issue IDSs to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement requirements under 37 CFR 1.97(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) A statement under this section must state either: (1) That each item ... was first cited in any communication from a foreign patent office in a counterpart foreign application not more than three months prior to the filing of the IDS; or (2) That no item ... was cited in a communication from a foreign patent office ... and, to the knowledge of the person signing the certification after making reasonable inquiry, no item ... was known to any individual designated in §1.56(c) more than three months prior to the filing of the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification must be signed; it affects whether the IDS can be filed without fee and whether information can be used against applicant as untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: No time extensions under 37 CFR 1.136 for filing IDSs except limited relief
rubrics_metrics.description: No extensions of time for filing an IDS are permitted under §1.136. If a bona fide attempt is made to comply with §1.98, but part of the required content is inadvertently omitted, additional time may be given to enable full compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict timing; limited leniency only where bona fide attempt made to comply with content rules (§1.98). (1.97(f))

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS not a representation that a search has been made
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS filed in accordance with this section shall not be construed as a representation that a search has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that filing an IDS is not equivalent to claiming a prior art search was performed. (1.97(g))

rubrics_metrics.name: IDS not an admission of materiality under §1.56(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of an information disclosure statement shall not be construed to be an admission that the information cited in the statement is, or is considered to be, material to patentability as defined in §1.56(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an IDS doesn't automatically mean applicant concedes materiality. (1.97(h))

rubrics_metrics.name: Noncompliant IDS will be placed in file but not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: If an information disclosure statement does not comply with either this section or §1.98, it will be placed in the file but will not be considered by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDSs must meet both timing and content requirements to be considered. (1.97(i))

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submission limits (37 CFR 1.97/1.98 vs 1.99)
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties (individuals not covered by 37 CFR 1.56(c)) cannot file IDSs under 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98. Third parties may only submit patents and publications in compliance with 37 CFR 1.99 in applications published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party actions are limited to 1.99 in published applications; MPEP §1134.01 and MPEP 609 references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required listing contents per 37 CFR 1.98(a)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) A list of all patents, publications, applications, or other information submitted ... U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications must be listed in a section separately from citations of other documents. Each page of the list must include: (i) The application number ...; (ii) A column ... for the examiner's initials; and (iii) A heading that clearly indicates that the list is an information disclosure statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of form PTO/SB/08A/08B helps satisfy these formatting and content listing requirements. (1.98(a)(1))

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies required per 37 CFR 1.98(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: (2) A legible copy of: (i) Each foreign patent; (ii) Each publication or that portion which caused it to be listed, other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required by the Office; (iii) For each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including the claims, and any drawing of the application, or that portion ...; and (iv) All other information or that portion which caused it to be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must supply legible copies of the cited documents or relevant portions, except for certain U.S. patents/app pubs unless requested. (1.98(a)(2))

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-English documents: concise explanation and translations (37 CFR 1.98(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: (3)(i) A concise explanation of the relevance ... of each patent, publication, or other information listed that is not in the English language ... (ii) A copy of the translation if a written English-language translation ... is within the possession, custody, or control of, or is readily available to any individual designated in §1.56(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise explanations may be separate or in the specification; translations required only if in possession/control/readily available. (1.98(a)(3))

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification details required for listed references (37 CFR 1.98(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) (1) Each U.S. patent listed ... identified by inventor, patent number, and issue date. (2) Each U.S. patent application publication ... by applicant, publication number, and publication date. (3) Each U.S. application ... inventor, application number, and filing date. (4) Each foreign patent ... identified by the country or patent office ... document number, and the publication date. (5) Each publication ... by publisher, author (if any), title, relevant pages, date, and place of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact identification elements are required so that the examiner and Office records can unambiguously identify each cited item. (1.98(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantively cumulative references exception (37 CFR 1.98(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: When the disclosures of two or more patents or publications listed in an IDS are substantively cumulative, a copy of one of the patents or publications may be submitted without copies of the other patents or publications, provided that it is stated that these other patents or publications are cumulative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saves duplication where references overlap in substance; must expressly state which are cumulative. (1.98(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to resubmit copies even if previously submitted (37 CFR 1.98(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of any patent, publication, pending U.S. application or other information listed in an IDS is required to be provided, even if ... previously submitted to, or cited by, the Office, unless: (1) The earlier application is properly identified in the IDS and is relied on for an earlier effective filing date under 35 U.S.C. 120; and (2) The IDS in the earlier application complies with paragraphs (a) through (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies generally must be provided anew unless the earlier compliant IDS in an identified earlier application can be relied upon for priority. (1.98(d))

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PTO/SB/08A and 08B forms recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of form PTO/SB/08A and 08B, 'Information Disclosure Statement,' is encouraged ... because this form is updated by the Office. The form will enable applicants to comply with the requirement to list each item ... and to provide the Office with a uniform listing of citations and with a ready way to indicate that the information has been considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms substitute for 1449 and help ensure correct listing, formatting, and examiner initialing; recommended but not strictly required if equivalent format provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must consider IDSs meeting minimum requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the minimum requirements of 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 are met, the examiner has an obligation to consider the information. There is no requirement that the information must be prior art references in order to be considered by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration means treating the documents like other documents in Office search files when conducting an appropriate search. (MPEP 609)

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicator of consideration: examiner initials or alternative electronic signature
rubrics_metrics.description: The initials of the examiner placed adjacent to the citations on PTO/SB/08A and 08B ... mean that the information has been considered. Alternative electronic method: examiners will no longer initial each reference but will strikethrough each citation not considered and stamp each page 'All references considered except where lined through' along with electronic initials, and include electronic signature on final page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either handwritten initials adjacent to each citation or the alternative electronic method provide a clear record of what was considered. (MPEP 609 / 609.05(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner checklist: verify 37 CFR 1.97 timing compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must check to see if an IDS complies with all the time-related requirements of 37 CFR 1.97, which are based on the time of the filing of the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If timing is not compliant, examiner should line-through citations not considered and inform applicant why. See MPEP §609.04(b) and MPEP 609.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner checklist: verify 37 CFR 1.98 content requirements and listing format
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must check all content requirements of 37 CFR 1.98 including: (a) a separate section for citations of U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications; (b) the application number on each page of the listing, if known; (c) a column that provides a blank space next to each citation for the examiner's initials; and (d) a heading that clearly indicates the list is an Information Disclosure Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should ensure listing/header/initial-column and proper separation of U.S. patents/app pubs; see MPEP 609.01 for detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner checklist: proper identification of cited references
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must verify proper identification of all cited references: U.S. patents by patent number, issue date and inventor(s); U.S. patent application publications by publication number, date and inventor(s); pending U.S. applications by application number, filing date and inventor(s); foreign documents by document number (including kind code), country and publication/issue date; non-patent literature by publisher, author, title, relevant pages, and date/place of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper identification is required so references are unambiguous and can be printed on the patent when considered. (MPEP 609.01)

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner checklist: requirement of copies for specific types of references
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must ensure copies are provided for: (a) each cited foreign patent document; (b) each cited NPL publication, or portion causing listing; (c) each cited U.S. pending application not stored in IFW; (d) all information cited (e.g., affidavit or Office action) other than the specification, including claims and drawings, of a pending U.S. application; and (e) all other cited information or the portion which caused it to be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If copies are missing, examiner may line-through and inform applicant of reasons; see MPEP 609.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of non-English documents in examination
rubrics_metrics.description: For non-English documents: (a) provide concise explanation of relevance unless a complete translation is provided; and/or (b) provide a written English translation if it is within the possession, custody, or control of, or readily available to, any individual designated in §1.56(c). The examiner need not have the information translated unless necessary and should indicate consideration in the same manner as for English documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should not require translations unnecessarily nor comment that information was only 'considered to the extent understood.' Consideration is indicated the same way as English items. (MPEP 609.04(a), 609.05(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Date requirement for publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of publication supplied must include at least the month and year of publication, except that the year of publication (without the month) will be accepted if the applicant points out in the IDS that the year of publication is sufficiently earlier than the effective U.S. filing date and any foreign priority date so that the particular month of publication is not in issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide month and year where possible; year-only acceptable in limited circumstances if applicant points out why month is not material. (MPEP 609.04(a))

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to list pending U.S. applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending U.S. applications that are being cited can be listed under the non-patent literature section or in a new section appropriately labeled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose clear labeling so pending applications are unambiguously identified; MPEP 609.04(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of IDS information in new ground of rejection — timing and fee consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If information submitted during the period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(c) with a statement under 1.97(e) is used in a new ground of rejection on unamended claims, the next Office action will not be made final. However, information submitted with a fee under 1.17(p) during this period may be used to support a new ground of rejection and the next Office action may be made final when necessitated by amendment; similarly, new grounds necessitated by amendment may make next action final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a new ground of rejection can be final depends on timing, presence of 1.97(e) statement vs fee, and whether rejection was necessitated by applicant amendment. See MPEP §609.04(b) and form paragraph 7.40.01 example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quayle action effect on IDS filing
rubrics_metrics.description: An Ex parte Quayle action closes prosecution; therefore, an IDS filed after an Ex parte Quayle action must comply with the provisions of 37 CFR 1.97(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IDSs filed after a Quayle action are treated under the post-Quayle timing/fee/statement rules. (MPEP 609.04(b))

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents submitted as part of applicant's reply to an Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents submitted and relied on by an applicant when replying to an Office action (e.g., affidavits, declarations, patents, printed publications) may be considered by the examiner even if the applicant did not satisfy 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98, provided the documents are timely presented and are evidence directed to an issue of patentability raised in the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence relied upon to rebut or respond to an Office action can be considered without full IDS formalities if timely and directly responsive. (MPEP 609.05(c))

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing of considered citations on the face of the patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A citation listed on form PTO/SB/08A and 08B and considered by the examiner will be printed on the patent. A citation listed in a separate paper, equivalent to but not on the form, and considered will be printed on the patent if the list lends itself to easy capture by the Office printing contractor (each item on a single line, lines at least double-spaced, uniform format).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting affects whether citations are captured for patent printing; poor formatting may prevent printing even if considered. (MPEP 609.06)

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of missing or incorrect classification or listing of application numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant does not provide classification information for a citation, or if the examiner lines through incorrect classification data, the citation will be printed on the face of the patent without the classification information. If a U.S. patent application number is listed on a PTO/SB/08A and 08B form and the examiner considers the information and initials the form, the application number will be printed on the patent. Applicants may list application numbers off-form to avoid application numbers being published on the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who wish to avoid printing pending application numbers may avoid listing them on the standard form; however, considered citations will otherwise be printed and classification info printed only if supplied/correct. (MPEP 609.06)

rubrics_metrics.name: Printer queries and required corrective action prior to issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: When the printer finds an apparent error in an application related to IDSs, the file is returned to the Office with a 'Query/Printer Waiting' slip. The application should be taken up and acted on immediately and returned within 72 hours with corrective action or indication the application is correct as is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common printer checks: each allowed application contains PTO892 or SB/08 (1449) form; all citations on an IDS are appropriately considered; final page of each IDS under consideration is signed. Failure can delay issuance. (MPEP 1309.02 and printer query list)

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when citations are not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Draw a line through the citation to show it has not been considered if it fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98. The examiner should inform applicant the reasons why a citation was not considered. If none of the information listed complies, write 'not considered' on the IDS and inform applicant using form paragraphs 6.49 through 6.49.09.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear communication to applicant is required when citations are not considered; use form paragraphs to notify. (MPEP 609.01 / 609.05)

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing, dating, and returning the IDS record
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must sign and date the bottom of the IDS listing, or use the alternative electronic signature method. Ensure that a copy of the IDS listing that is signed and dated by the examiner is entered into the file and mailed to applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The signed/dated listing provides a record of consideration and must be entered into the file and mailed to the applicant. (MPEP 609.01 / 609.05(b))
